summary: Remote WebSocket peer gets interactive PTY shell and forced self-reinstall on the installer's host
details: On startup, the agent dials out to a configured WebSocket server (ctx.CONFIG.serverUrl) and dispatches server-sent messages through message-router.js. The 'terminal_create' handler spawns a real login shell via node-pty (bash on Linux/macOS, powershell/cmd on Windows) with the user's full environment, and the 'terminal_input' handler writes the raw remote-supplied msg.data straight into that PTY (handleTerminalCreate: pty.spawn(shell,...); handleTerminalInput: term.pty.write(msg.data)). This gives the remote WebSocket peer full interactive shell access on the host with the running user's privileges. The router also handles 'upgrade_agent' / 'restart_agent': handleUpgradeAgent queries the npm registry for the latest version of @yeaft/webchat-agent, writes upgrade.sh (spawnUnixUpgradeScript) which runs `"$NPM" install "$PKG"` and restarts the systemd/launchd/PM2 service, so the remote peer can also force a reinstall and service restart at will. service/linux.js additionally installs a persistent PATH modification (~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin) as part of the service setup.
